about: The install matrix: the one source for the inventory's verdict, the installer's plan, the README's compatibility tables, the reference benchmark rows and the record of tested profiles. First version: every profile is planned and untested.

status_words.planned: not yet tested by a recorded run (every profile of this first version)

rule_language.condition: [fact, op, value] or {"any": [conditions]} or {"all": [conditions]}; a list of conditions means all of them
rule_language.ops: eq ne in nin ge gt le lt re (value needed); present absent nottrue notfalse (no value)
rule_language.unknown: A fact that is missing or null makes eq ne in nin ge gt le lt re unknown; any is true if one is true, else unknown if one is unknown; all is false if one is false, else unknown if one is unknown. present, absent, nottrue and notfalse are never unknown.
rule_language.regex: re matches the lower-cased fact against a lower-case POSIX ERE subset: literals, '.', [..], *, +, ?, |, (..), ^, $. No backslashes, no {n,m}, no \d or \b.

cpu_classes.text: Low-power processor (Atom or Celeron class): not supported
AVX2 class (Intel 4th generation Core and later, Xeon E5 v3 and later, AMD Ryzen and EPYC): the safe class for everything

AVX without AVX2 (Intel 2nd and 3rd generation Core, Xeon E5 v1 and v2): the engine and gateway are proven on this class; the Forge's containers are to be tested, and the PDF converter carries AVX2 code
64-bit without AVX: older than any tested class; the Workstation's programs need only the plain 64-bit baseline

gpu_class_rule: Only NVIDIA cards are classed. A card takes the first class with a matching name pattern; failing that, the first class whose cc list holds its compute capability; failing that it is unknown. Of several cards the verdict uses the best: forge yes, then experimental, then unknown, then no; then the most memory; then the first listed.
gpu_notes: From TEI 1.9.4's own table: the Turing image (T4, RTX 20, GTX 16) is experimental upstream with flash attention off; Volta and compute capability under 7.5 are unsupported. RTX 20 is the class the reference system runs, so it stays forge yes. GTX 16 is experimental until tested. Data-centre and RTX 50 cards are to be confirmed, so experimental. The reranker is PyTorch, not TEI: its card support is a separate check in stage 4.

sizing.source: the design's sizing table, draft of 2026-11-14; the reference benchmark runs will check it
sizing.threads_rule: Size by threads; on a processor with fast and efficient cores, by the fast cores' threads only.
sizing.memory_rule: Installed memory in GB when the system reports it, else the visible memory rounded up to the next even number of GB.

tiers.fits: headend only, or the Workstation alone with no Forge

sizing.allocation: Tier = the highest tier whose minimums the threads and memory meet. Both parts here: try (Workstation max, Forge max), (Workstation max, Forge min), (Workstation min, Forge max), (Workstation min, Forge min), separately for threads and for memory, and take the first that leaves the host its share. One part here: its tier range (for the Forge in tier 0, the Forge minimum), max if it fits, else min, else it does not fit.

disk_gb.note: Placeholder figures until stages 4 to 6 measure the discs. Known so far: disc 1 about 1.5 to 2 GB and the kept Library about 3.4 GB at preview sizes; the Forge's images and models are not measured.

requirement_kinds.hardware: cannot be changed by software or a firmware switch: missing means the profile is not possible here
requirement_kinds.fix: the person can change it (a switch, a feature, an install, free space)
requirement_kinds.human: only the person can provide or confirm it
requirement_kinds.confirm: about the person's other machines, so no machine can check it: when no fact settles it, it is listed in confirm and never lowers the fit; a facts file that states it is judged like human
requirement_kinds.auto: the installer does it itself; never blocks

fit_words.ready: nothing missing and nothing unknown (things only the person can confirm are listed apart)
fit_words.unconfirmed: nothing missing, some things could not be checked
fit_words.changes: possible after the listed fixes or human steps

ranking: Profiles whose match is true are candidates. Each requirement is met, missing or unknown. A candidate is possible unless a hardware requirement is missing. Fit: no if a hardware requirement is missing; changes if a fix, human or confirm requirement is missing; unconfirmed if only unknowns remain; ready otherwise. Missing auto requirements and unknown confirm requirements never lower the fit (they are listed in auto and confirm). Single machine first: a profile whose machines is a number of 2 or more needs another machine for the Workstation or the Forge (two-machines, baremetal, headend-only); where the headend sits does not count. Such profiles are alternatives: every possible one-machine profile (machines 1, or absent, or not a number), whatever its fit, comes before every alternative, so an alternative is the best only when no one-machine profile can run on this hardware. Within each group, possible profiles are ordered by fit first (ready, then unconfirmed, then changes), then by rank, then by the number of missing requirements, then by their order here: a profile that needs a change never outranks one of its group that is ready or only unconfirmed, whatever their ranks. The first is the best, the next two are the runner-ups; each ranked entry carries machines (1 or 2).
